messages:
Aisha Bello: Heads up: I pulled latest dashboards from observability-pack (pr_289) into staging. Quick sanity pass on the tiered batching views ✅. Anyone else able to spot-check before we call it “good”? Links:
- Grafana (staging): https://grafana.staging.redwood.ai/d/rt-batching-tiers
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-pack/pull/289

Felix Schneider: I checked the JSON import on the runtime folder. No errors on load. Panels render and variables look wired.

Sergio Costa: Looking now. The “Queue delay (p95) by tier” graph finally matches what runtime is emitting (labels show `batching_tier=fast|standard|cost_efficient`). :thumbsup:

Allison Grant: +1. The new breakdowns (prefill vs decode vs queue) are super helpful. I also verified the legend isn’t exploding cardinality (it’s grouping by model_family + tier, not per model_id).

Rafael Mendes: I’m mostly happy, but I’m worried about alert noise once we ramp beta.

Right now the alert in staging is firing constantly on cost_efficient during normal evening load. It’s triggering on p95 queue delay > 30ms for 5m. That seems too tight given we *expect* queueing there.

Chloe Martin: Is that the “Tier SLO guardrail” alert or the “Queue delay regression” one?

Rafael Mendes: The regression one. It’s in the new pack under `runtime/batching/alerts`. It pages in on-call rotation right now.

Grafana Bot: Alert firing: `batching_queue_delay_p95_regression`
- Severity: page
- Labels: tier=cost_efficient, region=us-east-1, model_family=llama
- Value: 47.2ms (threshold 30ms)

Sergio Costa: Yeah, I see it. The graph shows cost_efficient p95 queue delay hovering 40–60ms but end-to-end p95 is still inside the cost_efficient SLO band.

Maybe the queue delay alert should be tier-aware (fast should be strict, cost_efficient should be looser) OR demoted to warn.

Allison Grant: Agree. Queue delay is a leading indicator, but paging on it for cost_efficient feels wrong. We should page on e2e SLO miss + error rate changes.

Aisha Bello: Proposed change:
- For `fast`: keep p95 queue delay threshold as-is (30ms) but require sustained 10m
- For `standard`: 60ms / 10m (warn)
- For `cost_efficient`: 120ms / 15m (warn)
- Keep separate “tail latency SLO miss” alert as page (per tier)

That aligns with what we wrote in the batching standards doc.

Felix Schneider: I can push an update to the alert rules in observability-pack today. Can someone paste the exact query you want? Current is:

```
histogram_quantile(0.95,
  sum(rate(runtime_queue_delay_ms_bucket{service="inference"}[5m])) by (le, batching_tier, region, model_family)
)
```

Rafael Mendes: Query is fine. It’s the thresholds + severity that need tier awareness.

We can implement as three alerts (one per tier) with different thresholds. Also add `for:` durations.

Sergio Costa: +1. Also can we exclude embeddings route? It has very different queue behavior and is triggering the same alert sometimes.

Allison Grant: If we split, we can also add `route!="embeddings"` for the chat/completions one, and a separate embeddings-specific alert if needed (probably warn only).

Aisha Bello: Works for me. Let’s not overcomplicate: for beta, exclude embeddings from the regression page path.

Felix Schneider: Cool. I’ll update rules:
- Split by tier
- cost_efficient + standard => warn
- fast => page
- add route filter to exclude embeddings

Will post PR link here.

Logan Wright: Minor note: make sure the label is `route` not `endpoint` in the new metrics. Runtime changed that last month.

Felix Schneider: Good catch. I’ll validate in staging Prometheus.

Chloe Martin: Once thresholds are updated, can we also update the dashboard annotation? Right now it says “queue delay should be <30ms” which is only true for fast.

Aisha Bello: Yes please. Add a note in the dashboard text panel: “Queue delay expectations vary by tier; see alerts panel / docs.”

Rafael Mendes: Thank you. This will save us from a lot of false pages during the ramp.

Felix Schneider: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-pack/pull/294
- Tier-aware thresholds
- Severity adjustments
- `route!="embeddings"` filter

Please review.

Sergio Costa: Reviewed and LGTM. :thumbsup:

Allison Grant: LGTM as well. One tiny nit: add `for: 10m` on the fast page alert (I think you set 5m). Otherwise good.

Felix Schneider: Updated to 10m.

Aisha Bello: Approved. Once merged + deployed, I’ll re-check staging and then we can mark the dashboards/alerts as ready for beta monitoring checklist.

Grafana Bot: Alert resolved: `batching_queue_delay_p95_regression`
